## Exercise 1 (15 points)

For each scenario, write out the appropriate null and alternative hypothesis **in proper notation**.

a)  A professor wants to know if the average exam score for her class is different from the historical average of 80 on a standardized test. She believes her class will perform differently due to a new teaching method.

b)  A space agency wants to compare the reliability of two different private companies, Provider A and Provider B, for launching satellites into orbit. The agency collects data on their recent launch history. Provider A has completed 200 launches, with 192 of them being successful. Provider B has completed 150 launches, with 138 of them being successful. The space agency wants to investigate if Provider B has less safe launches, as they tend to user older technologies.

c)  A politician claims that they have an approval rating of at least 50%. A political analyst wants to test this claim and believes the true approval rating is lower.

## Exercise-2

A veterinarian wants to determine whether the proportion of dogs that experience seasonal allergies differs between two breeds. A random sample of 150 Labrador Retrievers is examined, and 45 are found to experience seasonal allergies. A random sample of 150 Golden Retrievers is examined, and 60 are found to experience seasonal allergies.

Is there evidence that the proportion of dogs experiencing seasonal allergies differs between Labrador Retrievers and Golden Retrievers? Use a significance level of $\alpha=0.05$ to answer this question.

a. Define $p_l$ and $p_g$ in words in the context of the problem. 

b. Our null and alternative hypotheses can be seen below: 
$H_o: p_l = p_g$

$H_a: p_l \neq p_g$

The researcher wants to calculate the probability of making a Type-2 error, and the Power of their test. Below, report the values from the context of the problem that we will need to make these calculations. Show your work if necessary. 

-   $n_g$ = 

-   $n_l$ = 

-   $SE(p_{\text{l-null}} - p_{\text{g-null}})$ = 

c. Please see the following visualization to answer the following question: 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(ggplot2)

# Parameters
null_mean <- 0
alternative_mean <- 0.20
se <- 0.05
alpha <- 0.05

# Critical values
critical_left <- qnorm(alpha / 2, mean = null_mean, sd = se)
critical_right <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2, mean = null_mean, sd = se)

# Create data
x <- seq(-0.25, 0.40, length.out = 1000)

data <- data.frame(
  x = x,
  null = dnorm(x, mean = null_mean, sd = se),
  alternative = dnorm(x, mean = alternative_mean, sd = se)
)

ggplot(data, aes(x = x)) +
  
  # Null distribution
  geom_line(aes(y = null), linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Alternative distribution
  geom_line(aes(y = alternative), 
            linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  
  # Type I error - left tail
  geom_area(
    data = subset(data, x <= critical_left),
    aes(y = null),
    fill = "red",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  
  # Type I error - right tail
  geom_area(
    data = subset(data, x >= critical_right),
    aes(y = null),
    fill = "red",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  
  # Type II error
  geom_area(
    data = subset(data, x >= critical_left & x <= critical_right),
    aes(y = alternative),
    fill = "blue",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  
  # Power - right rejection region
  geom_area(
    data = subset(data, x >= critical_right),
    aes(y = alternative),
    fill = "green",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  
  # Critical values
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(critical_left, critical_right),
    linetype = "dotted",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "Difference in Proportions",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal()
```

## Exercise 4 (5 points)

A large retail store tracks customer complaints to determine if the volume of complaints is evenly distributed across the five primary days of the work week (Monday through Friday). The management's null hypothesis is that the complaints occur with equal frequency on all five days. We want to determine if the observed distribution of complaints significantly differs from the expected uniform distribution.

a.  In 2-4 sentences, explain the difference between a goodness of fit test, and a test for independence AND specify which test would be most appropriate for the scenario above.
